messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden rise in 5xx for /v1/generate in us-west-2. error_rate ~20% starting 23:05 UTC. paging primary on-call: @maria. Please acknowledge.

maria (oncall): ack 23:06 UTC. I'm seeing 503/502 across several worker shards.

jon (sre): joining. pulling kube/node metrics. network looks fine, but host mem pressure high and many runtime processes restarting.

sam (runtime): any infra changes in the last hour?

deploy-bot: infra: kernel patch deploy `kp-abc123` applied to runtime fleet at 22:58 UTC. No application deploys.

maria (oncall): thanks. jon, can you surface logs for the runtime workers?

jon (sre): tailing logs—pattern: repeated KV cache evictions followed by OOM kills, then worker restarts. snippet: `KVCache::evict count=1200 mem_free=0` then `oom_kill` for process `llm-worker`.

sam (runtime): that smells like allocator behavior change after kernel tweak. I ran quick local tests earlier and saw prefault/alloc stalls.

maria (oncall): immediate mitigations we can try: 1) reduce batch sizes for busy pools, 2) throttle new requests to the region, 3) rollback kernel patch if needed. preferences?

jon (sre): I'll trigger emergency autoscale to add capacity and apply a temporary per-pool concurrency cap. pushing config: max_batch_size=12 for affected pools.

maria (oncall): do it. open a rollback queue in case autoscale + batch caps don't recover in 10m.

deploy-bot: rollback plan available: `rollback-kp-abc123` per infra runbook; can be executed per-rack.

nina (cs): heads up — a handful of high-impact accounts are reporting errors via support. tagging @tara for external messaging.

tara (product): I can draft a short status blurb. keep it factual and concise.

jon (sre): 23:14 UTC — autoscale + batch cap applied. error rate down from 20% to ~7% but still elevated.

sam (runtime): starting rolling restart of worst-performing runtime nodes to clear allocator state.

olivia (support): queued customer notifications for accounts with >100 failed requests. will hold send until PM approves wording.

jon (sre): 23:22 UTC — rolled back kernel patch on rack-4 as a canary. post-rollback metrics on rack-4 look normal within 60s.

maria (oncall): good sign. proceed to rollbacks across racks until region stabilizes. keep autoscale until we confirm.

sam (runtime): confirming: reproduction locally against kp-abc123 shows increased fragmentation and delayed reclaim under concurrent mmap/prefaults. allocator ends up thrashing. I'll work up a minimal repro and a runtime mitigation (tighter cache eviction thresholds) by EOD.

maria (oncall): 23:38 UTC — region error rate returned to baseline (~1%). declaring incident mitigated. moving to post-incident actions.

incident-bot: UPDATE: incident mitigated at 23:38 UTC. Please complete post-incident checklist and schedule postmortem within 72 hours.

maria (oncall): quick incident summary: root cause likely interaction between kernel patch kp-abc123 and our runtime allocator causing excessive KV-cache evictions -> OOMs -> 5xx. mitigations applied: rack-level rollback of kp-abc123, emergency autoscale, reduced batch sizes, rolling runtime restarts.

jon (sre): action items — I'll add these to the incident tracker: 1) add mem-pressure and eviction-rate alerting; 2) document rollback playbook improvements; 3) verify rollback durability with autoscaling flows. (owner: jon)

sam (runtime): action items from runtime: 1) reproduce and root-cause the allocator regression against kp-abc123, produce a small repro; 2) propose runtime config hardening to avoid thrash under prefault; 3) add unit/integration test for kernel-change plume. (owner: sam)

kevin (eng-lead): add: require kernel patch canary gating tied to runtime health metrics before broad rollout. (owner: kevin)

tara (product): external comms: drafting status page entry. here's a short draft — please comment: 

---STATUS DRAFT---
We experienced increased 5xx errors for the Redwood API in US-West between 23:05 and 23:38 UTC. The incident was caused by an infrastructure kernel update that impacted memory allocation behavior on runtime hosts, causing cache thrashing and service errors. We mitigated by rolling back the kernel update, adding capacity, and applying temporary runtime config limits. Service has been restored. A full RCA and timeline will be published within 72 hours.
---END---

nina (cs): add sentence: "No customer data was exposed; this incident affected availability only." then send.

olivia (support): approved from support side. will coordinate targeted messages for accounts in the high-impact list once Tara posts final.

maria (oncall): scheduling postmortem meeting: propose tomorrow 14:00 UTC. required attendees: sam, jon, kevin, tara, nina, maria, oncall rotation.

jon (sre): 14:00 UTC works.

sam (runtime): available.

kevin (eng-lead): I'll join.

tara (product): ok.

nina (cs): ok.

maria (oncall): created postmortem doc placeholder: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/2330001111-kernel-memory-regression — please populate timeline, logs, and action owners before the meeting.

tara (product): customer trust and remediation plan suggestions: 1) targeted 1:1 outreach to top affected accounts within 24h (owner: nina); 2) offer one month of prioritized support and weekly status updates to impacted enterprise customers (owner: tara); 3) consider service credit for accounts with >5% error impact or critical SLAs (owner: sales); 4) publish public postmortem on status page after PM review (owner: tara).

nina (cs): I'll draft outreach emails and coordinate with sales for credit approval flow.

jon (sre): I'll create tickets in the incident tracker for alerting, runbook updates, and kernel gating. link: https://tracker.redwood/incidents/2330001111

maria (oncall): final operational notes: 1) confirm rollback persists across scale events; 2) ensure kernel rollout pipeline has runtime canary gates; 3) get deterministic repro from sam to allow a non-rollback fix.

sam (runtime): will upload repro and proposed runtime patch into the postmortem doc before the meeting.

olivia (support): once status page goes live, I'll send customer summaries and attach to affected account threads.

kevin (eng-lead): please prepare a one-page exec summary for leadership review post-mortem. I'll review before we publish.

maria (oncall): closing the active pager. please add any missed follow-ups to the tracker.

incident-bot: Incident closed at 23:44 UTC. Postmortem scheduled for 14:00 UTC next day. Reminder: publish RCA within 72 hours. (reactions: :thumbsup:, :heart:)
